state: local draft requiring assets and integration review

course.title: Create your first UniVybe course
course.short_description: A practical course creation manual for educators and tutors.
course.description: Plan, build, preview and prepare a course for approval using UniVybe modules, lessons, mini-lessons, content blocks and quizzes.
learning_objectives: Select each supported text and media format
Check the learner experience and prepare a course for review
prerequisites: Access to an approved educator or tutor account
A topic to teach and permission to use its learning materials

modules.title: Plan a course learners can complete
modules.description: Define the audience and a useful outcome.

lessons.title: Choose the audience and outcome
lessons.description: Write an observable outcome and a small course outline.
learning_objectives: Write an observable outcome and a small course outline.

mini_lessons.title: Choose the audience and outcome
mini_lessons.description: Write an observable outcome and a small course outline.

blocks.content: Start with what an educator or tutor should be able to do after the course. For this manual, the outcome is to create, preview and submit a complete UniVybe course with appropriate content and quizzes.

Write outcomes using actions you can observe: create, explain, solve or demonstrate. For example: Create one module containing a lesson, a mini-lesson, content blocks and a quiz. Avoid an outcome such as Understand everything about teaching.

Identify what learners already know, what they need to bring, and which device they will use. Keep each lesson focused on one outcome. Estimate the time only after drafting and walking through the activities.

Try it yourself
Write a course title, target audience, two learning objectives and one prerequisite. Sketch two modules with one focused lesson in each.

lessons.title: Understand the UniVybe course structure
lessons.description: Put each item in the correct place in the course outline.
learning_objectives: Put each item in the correct place in the course outline.

mini_lessons.title: Understand the UniVybe course structure
mini_lessons.description: Put each item in the correct place in the course outline.

blocks.content: A course is the full learning experience. Modules divide it into topics. Lessons sit inside modules. Mini-lessons divide each lesson into focused screens. Text and media blocks sit inside a mini-lesson.
Quizzes belong directly to a lesson, alongside its mini-lessons. They do not belong inside a content block. The student player builds screens from mini-lessons and quizzes.
The Academic module field in course details links an official university registry entry. It is different from the modules you create as chapters in this course.

Course → Module → Lesson → Mini-lesson → Content blocks
Lesson → Quizzes

Try it yourself
Draw your course tree and mark where a quiz belongs.

quizzes.question: Where do you add a quiz?
quizzes.explanation: A lesson holds mini-lessons and quizzes.

modules.title: Create the draft and build the outline
modules.description: Create a small complete learning path before adding more material.

lessons.title: Create course details
lessons.description: Save a course draft with clear learner facing information.
learning_objectives: Save a course draft with clear learner facing information.

mini_lessons.title: Create course details
mini_lessons.description: Save a course draft with clear learner facing information.

blocks.content: Open Courses and create a course. Enter the title and description, then save. These are required in the current frontend. State who the course is for, what learners will do and what they need before starting. Use the short description as a concise summary.

Choose General for a broad audience, or the appropriate academic level. Not set leaves the level unspecified. Add university, faculty, department, organization or an official academic module only when relevant; an organization course does not require a university context.

Add learning objectives, prerequisites and tags using one item per line. Add a cover URL or use the upload controls where available. Check that the image is readable on a small screen and that you have permission to use it.

Estimated hours and lesson or quiz counts describe the intended scope. Check them against the final outline. Pricing and coin rewards entered by creators are suggestions; an admin sets final pricing and rewards.

Try it yourself
Create a practice draft with a specific title, a useful description and two learning objectives. Save it and confirm that it appears in Courses.

lessons.title: Build modules lessons and mini lessons
lessons.description: Save and reorder a module containing one complete lesson.
learning_objectives: Save and reorder a module containing one complete lesson.

mini_lessons.title: Build modules lessons and mini lessons
mini_lessons.description: Save and reorder a module containing one complete lesson.

blocks.content: In the course outline, choose Add module. Give it a topic title and save. Expand that module, choose Add lesson, set its title and lesson type, and save. Reading, video and mixed describe the lesson; media itself is added as content blocks.
Expand the lesson and choose Add mini-lesson. Give the screen a meaningful title and save. Expand it and choose Add content block. Add one plain text block first, save, then preview the course.

Each editor saves separately. Save before choosing a different outline item. Use the saved confirmation to distinguish a confirmed save from a retained unsaved draft. Moving away with unsaved changes opens a save or discard decision.
Use drag handles or Move up and Move down to reorder siblings. Order applies within the selected parent. After an interrupted reorder, reload and inspect the saved sequence before trying again.

Try it yourself
Build one module with a reading lesson and two mini-lessons. Add a text block to each, reorder them and verify the result in preview.

quizzes.question: What holds a lesson in the course outline? Answer with one singular word.

modules.title: Use every supported content type
modules.description: Choose a format that supports the learning task.

lessons.title: Write text explanations and reminders
lessons.description: Use the four explanation styles with a clear purpose.
learning_objectives: Use the four explanation styles with a clear purpose.

mini_lessons.title: Write text explanations and reminders
mini_lessons.description: Use the four explanation styles with a clear purpose.

blocks.content: Choose Content type text, then choose the text style. Plain is the default for explanations, instructions and worked examples. Break long passages into focused mini-lessons instead of placing the whole course in one block.

Simply put gives a simpler restatement after an explanation. Important highlights a consequence or condition. Remember reinforces something learners need to carry into the next activity. Keep these blocks brief so their emphasis remains useful.
A learning objective describes something the learner can demonstrate.
Write what the learner will do.
Only add media you are allowed to share with learners.
Save each content block before moving to another item.

Try it yourself
Teach one idea using plain text, then add a simpler restatement, one important condition and one reminder.

lessons.title: Add formulas links and copyable prompts
lessons.description: Create a formula a labelled link and a reusable prompt.
learning_objectives: Create a formula a labelled link and a reusable prompt.

mini_lessons.title: Add formulas links and copyable prompts
mini_lessons.description: Create a formula a labelled link and a reusable prompt.

blocks.content: For Formula, enter LaTeX and inspect the formula preview. For example, \frac{3}{4} teaches a fraction. Explain the symbols in a nearby plain text block so the formula is meaningful without relying only on the visual.

For Link, enter one complete HTTP or HTTPS address as the content. The optional label is limited to 100 characters on one line and must not contain a web address. Use Check link to confirm the destination. Put longer instructions in a preceding plain text block.

For Prompt, enter plain text learners can copy. Preserve useful line breaks and placeholders. State what to replace before using it, and check the student Copy prompt control. A prompt is a content format rather than a graded quiz.

Create three practice questions about [TOPIC].
Use beginner level language.
Explain each answer after I attempt it.

Try it yourself
Create a formula, a labelled course reference link and a prompt with a replaceable topic. Check their previews.

lessons.title: Add images video embeds and documents
lessons.description: Select and check each of the four media block types.
learning_objectives: Select and check each of the four media block types.

mini_lessons.title: Add images video embeds and documents
mini_lessons.description: Select and check each of the four media block types.

blocks.content: Choose Image for an illustration or screenshot. Add a valid media URL or use the lesson media upload controls. Add a caption using advanced metadata when needed. Explain essential visual information in an adjacent text block because captions are not a substitute for verified accessible alternatives.

Choose Video for a demonstration. Paste the media address, including a supported YouTube watch, share or embed URL, rather than iframe code. Provide a short text summary and an accessible transcript or captions, then check playback on desktop and mobile.

Choose Embed for an external interactive resource. Check that the provider allows embedding and that learners can access it without your account. Provide a link or written alternative if embedding is blocked.

Choose Document for a handout or reference file. Explain what learners should do with the file and test opening it as a learner. A document block displays or links media; course level resource attachments are managed separately.

The media URL is required for non-text blocks. Advanced media metadata accepts JSON. Leave existing metadata unchanged unless needed; do not erase unfamiliar saved properties. For a caption, an example is {"caption":"Course outline example"}.

Try it yourself
Add one image, one short video, one allowed embed and one document from your own approved materials. Test every address and include a text alternative.

modules.title: Build useful quizzes
modules.description: Create examples of every authorable quiz type.

lessons.title: Write multiple choice questions
lessons.description: Create questions with one or several correct choices.
learning_objectives: Create questions with one or several correct choices.

mini_lessons.title: Write multiple choice questions
mini_lessons.description: Create questions with one or several correct choices.

blocks.content: Expand a lesson and choose Add quiz. Choose Multiple choice, write a clear question, add at least two distinct choices and tick every correct choice. For a single correct answer, tick only one. For multiple correct answers, say Select all that apply in the question.

Use plausible incorrect choices that reveal a misunderstanding. Avoid trick wording or choices that differ only in punctuation. Add an explanation describing why the answer is correct and what the learner should revisit.

Open optional settings only when needed. A blank time limit means untimed. Empty reward and attempt fields keep existing values or use server defaults for new quizzes. These defaults need to be confirmed with the backend before making learner promises.

Try it yourself
Create one question with one correct choice and another with two correct choices. Inspect the answer key in preview.

quizzes.question: Select all items that belong directly to a lesson.
quizzes.explanation: Mini-lessons and quizzes belong to a lesson; blocks belong to mini-lessons.

lessons.title: Write short answer and one word questions
lessons.description: Choose accepted answers that fit the intended response.
learning_objectives: Choose accepted answers that fit the intended response.

mini_lessons.title: Write short answer and one word questions
mini_lessons.description: Choose accepted answers that fit the intended response.

blocks.content: Short answer accepts a short response and alternative wording. Add the main answer first and use Add alternative answer for valid variations. Keep the prompt specific enough that a short answer can demonstrate the outcome.
One word requires each accepted answer to be a single word. Use alternative answer rows for legitimate spelling or terminology variations. Do not add a sentence to this type.

These controls do not provide a teacher marked essay workflow. Avoid asking for a long explanation and expecting automatic grading. Check correct and incorrect answers in the student portal, including capitalization and spacing, before release.

Try it yourself
Write one short answer question and one one-word question. Enter a valid alternative answer for the short answer question.

quizzes.question: What should you do before leaving an edited block?
quizzes.explanation: Save the current editor before moving on.

quizzes.question: Which text style displays mathematical LaTeX?
quizzes.explanation: Use the formula text style for LaTeX.

lessons.title: Write fill in the blank and tap to fill questions
lessons.description: Keep blank answers and word bank choices in the intended order.
learning_objectives: Keep blank answers and word bank choices in the intended order.

mini_lessons.title: Write fill in the blank and tap to fill questions
mini_lessons.description: Keep blank answers and word bank choices in the intended order.

blocks.content: For Fill in the blank, write the sentence with blank spaces and enter answers in left to right blank order. Use Add blank answer for another position. Move the answer rows up or down to fix their order.
For Tap to fill, add the word bank first, then select the answer for each blank from that bank. Include useful distractors. Every selected answer must match a word bank entry.

The tutor form does not define a reliable blank marker or count blanks for you. Spaces at the start and end of the question are trimmed by the server. Keep blanks between visible text and verify their display and grading in the student portal. The draft includes both types for review, but their end to end release is gated on the compatibility checks in the review log.

Try it yourself
Create one two-blank question and one tap-to-fill question. Check answer order, then try correct and incorrect submissions in a controlled student session.

modules.title: Review submit and maintain the course
modules.description: Inspect the learner experience and record improvements.

lessons.title: Review the student experience
lessons.description: Complete a structured desktop and mobile review.
learning_objectives: Complete a structured desktop and mobile review.

mini_lessons.title: Review the student experience
mini_lessons.description: Complete a structured desktop and mobile review.

blocks.content: Use Preview course to inspect the saved content and answer review. This preview helps with authoring; it does not prove enrollment, grading, progress, media access or publication behavior in the student portal.

In a controlled student session, inspect the course summary, open the first lesson and read every mini-lesson. Test links, copy prompts, formulas and media on desktop and a small screen. Check text readability and whether the lesson order makes sense.

Try each quiz with correct, incorrect and alternative answers. Confirm the explanation, allowed attempts, next screen behavior and recorded progress. Check lesson completion and access to the next lesson. Do not treat the screenshots in the companion as proof of successful grading; they use illustrative data.

For each difficulty, record the exact action, what you expected, what happened and a suggested change. Separate missing content from an editor problem or student compatibility issue. Retest after each change.

Try it yourself
Walk through your practice course on desktop and mobile. Record at least one improvement with steps to reproduce and a clear expected result.

lessons.title: Submit a complete course for approval
lessons.description: Prepare a course for review and retain a maintenance checklist.
learning_objectives: Prepare a course for review and retain a maintenance checklist.

mini_lessons.title: Submit a complete course for approval
mini_lessons.description: Prepare a course for review and retain a maintenance checklist.

blocks.content: Check the title, description, objectives, prerequisites, counts and estimated time. Confirm every module, mini-lesson, block and quiz that should be visible is marked available where the form provides that setting. Saving a draft and enabling an item are separate from course approval.

Save the current editor before choosing Submit for approval. The creation portal submits the course for review and expects a pending approval status. An admin decision is required; submitting does not by itself make the course public.

After a review decision, inspect the returned status and feedback. Apply the requested corrections and follow the available submission workflow. If a save result is uncertain, use the check saved controls, inspect the server version and avoid repeating a create request that might duplicate content.

Before launch, resolve the quiz compatibility checks, replace all pending media and screenshots, and complete the controlled student walkthrough. Keep a dated record of content changes, broken link repairs and learner feedback.

Try it yourself
Prepare your course checklist and submit only when the actual course is complete. This local training draft remains unpublished.
